text: Straight men who have a lot of close female friends are actually a big green flag because it means that women feel safe enough around them to be their friend and know that they're not going to hit on them. Because, let's get real, men are not learning emotional intelligence from each other unless they have gay guy friends or female friends. Like, it's not happening. Oh boy, here we go again. According to her, straight men with lots of female friends are a big green flag because it supposedly means women feel safe, he is emotionally intelligent, and he is not trying to hit on anyone. My experience tells me that in real life the situation is way more controversial. In my opinion, having an army of female friends is not some magical green flag. And here's why. Most of the time, having a lot of female friends as a guy means having a lot of free time. Normally, the men who are successful in life and in dating are quite busy. They have work, careers, sports, hobbies, they see their bodies, and of course, they date women. They simply don't have time to maintain a circle of 10 female best friends. They can be in contact with many women because of work or hobbies, but that's more of acquaintances, not friends. Another problem is that guys who have a lot of female friends often get used for attention. Women use them as emotional support, therapists, backup plans, a safe space. But when it comes to attraction, these men get the classic, you are such a good friend. As a result, these men never develop the necessary self-respect and boundaries. They end up listening to advice on how to date women from women who don't understand dating from the male perspective. Ask yourself honestly, out of the men you look up to, the men you consider strong, stable, and admirable, how many of them strike you as guys with a huge group of female friends? Or is it more the men with purpose, hobbies, close male friends, and an actual dating life? Not endless conversations about how was her day and what is the problem with the new guy she is seeing. And the statement that men learn emotional intelligence only from women or gay men is absurd. Men also learn emotional intelligence from fathers, brothers, mentors, male friends, coaches, and from life. Being calm, solving problems, providing, protecting, and carrying responsibility is emotional intelligence in practice. So this whole men with lots of female friends are a green flag idea is far from the full truth. And in many cases, it backfires on men more than it helps them.
